title: Automated Logistics Manifest Verification
business: Logistics and warehouse distribution centers managing high-volume inbound freight.
problem: Manual verification of paper-based shipping manifests against physical pallet contents is error-prone, slow, and creates bottlenecks at loading docks.
solution: The Qwen3.5-4B model acts as a multimodal processing engine that ingests images of shipping manifests and physical pallet labels, cross-referencing the visual data with text-based order records to identify discrepancies automatically.
steps: Capture high-resolution images of incoming pallet labels and corresponding paper manifests.
Format the input using the model's vision-capable chat template to include image tokens.
Pass the combined image and text prompt to the Qwen3.5-4B inference endpoint.
Parse the model's structured text output to flag mismatches in item counts or SKU codes.
Route flagged discrepancies to human supervisors for manual inspection.
outcome: Increased throughput at receiving bays and improved accuracy in inventory logging by reducing reliance on manual data entry.
limitation: The model's performance on long-form, dense document analysis is constrained by its architecture; complex, multi-page manifests may lead to truncated or less accurate extraction. Verify accuracy by comparing model output against a subset of manually audited documents.
